import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    dim_acct = inputs["dim_acct"].copy()
    stg_acct = inputs["stg_acct"].copy()
    
    # Step 1: Dedup STG_ACCT to latest per acct_id by update_date
    # Ties: greater (email, tier) lexicographic pair wins
    stg_acct = stg_acct.sort_values(
        by=["acct_id", "update_date", "email", "tier"],
        ascending=[True, True, False, False],
        na_position="last"
    )
    stg_acct_dedup = stg_acct.drop_duplicates(subset=["acct_id"], keep="first")
    
    # Step 2: Process each staged record
    for _, staged_row in stg_acct_dedup.iterrows():
        s_acct_id = staged_row["acct_id"]
        s_email = staged_row["email"]
        s_tier = staged_row["tier"]
        s_update_date = staged_row["update_date"]
        
        # Find current row for this acct_id
        current_mask = (dim_acct["acct_id"] == s_acct_id) & (dim_acct["is_current"] == 1)
        current_rows = dim_acct[current_mask]
        
        if len(current_rows) == 0:
            # Insert new current version
            new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                "acct_id": [s_acct_id],
                "email": [s_email],
                "tier": [s_tier],
                "eff_start_date": [s_update_date],
                "eff_end_date": [pd.NaT],
                "is_current": [1]
            })
            dim_acct = pd.concat([dim_acct, new_row], ignore_index=True)
        else:
            # Current row exists
            current_row = current_rows.iloc[0]
            c_email = current_row["email"]
            c_tier = current_row["tier"]
            current_idx = current_rows.index[0]
            
            # Check for TYPE-2 change (tier change)
            # Use null-safe comparison: NULL vs NULL is same, NULL vs non-NULL is different
            tier_changed = (pd.isna(c_tier) and not pd.isna(s_tier)) or \
                          (not pd.isna(c_tier) and pd.isna(s_tier)) or \
                          (not pd.isna(c_tier) and not pd.isna(s_tier) and c_tier != s_tier)
            
            # Check for TYPE-1 change (email change)
            email_changed = (pd.isna(c_email) and not pd.isna(s_email)) or \
                           (not pd.isna(c_email) and pd.isna(s_email)) or \
                           (not pd.isna(c_email) and not pd.isna(s_email) and c_email != s_email)
            
            if tier_changed:
                # Expire current row at s_update_date
                dim_acct.loc[current_idx, "eff_end_date"] = s_update_date
                dim_acct.loc[current_idx, "is_current"] = 0
                
                # Insert new current version
                new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                    "acct_id": [s_acct_id],
                    "email": [s_email],
                    "tier": [s_tier],
                    "eff_start_date": [s_update_date],
                    "eff_end_date": [pd.NaT],
                    "is_current": [1]
                })
                dim_acct = pd.concat([dim_acct, new_row], ignore_index=True)
            
            if email_changed:
                # Retro-overwrite email across all rows of this acct_id
                dim_acct.loc[dim_acct["acct_id"] == s_acct_id, "email"] = s_email
    
    # Reset index for clean output
    dim_acct = dim_acct.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"dim_acct_out": dim_acct}
